marche_et_risque: TSLA is the most volatile asset in the available universe among individual stocks: its historical volatility reaches {vol_tsla}, well above comparable assets such as AAPL ({vol_aapl}) or MSFT ({vol_msft}). The concentration cap allowed for an individual security is {lim_max_titre_individuel}; an allocation of {lim_max_part_risquee} to a single security therefore exceeds this constraint by a very significant factor.

The worst drawdown observed on TSLA is {pb_tsla}. To simply return to the starting point after such a decline, the simulated portfolio would need to record a recovery gain of {rattrapage_tsla}. This is incompatible with a capital preservation objective over a three-year horizon.

AGG ({vol_agg}, {pb_agg}) and ZST.TO ({vol_zst_to}, {pb_zst_to}) are the least volatile assets in the available universe. Their correlation with TSLA is nearly zero ({corr_tsla_agg} for AGG), which makes them natural shock absorbers: increasing their weight in the simulated portfolio reduces overall exposure to shocks without concentrating risk.

GLD shows a very low correlation with TSLA ({corr_tsla_gld}) and a worst drawdown of {pb_gld}, considerably more contained than TSLA's. Defensive assets like ENB.TO ({vol_enb_to}), FTS.TO ({vol_fts_to}), and XIU.TO ({vol_xiu_to}) also show historically much lower risk profiles than TSLA and can help cushion the simulated portfolio.
macro: XBB.TO shows a rate sensitivity of {sens_xbb_to} and TLT of {sens_tlt}: a rise in rates weighs heavily on both of these bond ETFs, making them risky for a capital preservation objective over a short horizon.
ZST.TO has a sensitivity of only {sens_zst_to}: this short-term ETF reacts very little to rate movements and serves as a defensive anchor in a simulated portfolio.

The yield curve is positively sloped in Canada ({pente_canada}) as well as in the United States ({pente_tats_unis}), meaning long-term rates are above short-term rates; Eagle notes that the market is not pricing in an inversion, but that holding long-term bonds increases exposure to duration risk.
